I considered whether that second clause reopens the door to a composed grant and concluded it does not — clause 2 forbids re-recording the D-054 quotations, and the disposition forbids a coordinator draft minting (A), so 'records such words' can only mean words the user actually says.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. I offered two repairs at turn 1 — produce the user's actual words, or withdraw and leave D-096 (A) unsatisfied — and the entry takes the second, which is the harder one, since it leaves the completion path blocked with nothing gained. It withdraws rather than rephrases, and a rejected alternative says why rephrasing would not have worked: same words, same D-054 confinement. The quotation block is deleted rather than re-punctuated, which answers my SHOULD-FIX more completely than fixing the ellipses would have. Two things are worth recording beyond the findings. Both reviewers reached this defect independently without access to each other's files, which is the strongest signal this protocol produces. And the entry leaves behind a usable statement of the principle — a coordinator draft under review cannot mint its own authorising grant — which is the same proposition that produced D-054's present form and is now recorded twice.
